newsitem.title: USA: CheckFree starts two-way computer billing service.
newsitem.headline: CheckFree starts two-way computer billing service.

text.p: CheckFree Corp. Tuesday introduced CheckFree E-Bill, an Internet-based service that allows consumers to both receive and pay bills electronically through a personal computer.
This allows companies to lower billing costs by as much as one-third, Checkfree said.

BellSouth, Columbia Gas, Florida Power & Light, Consumers Energy and The CUNA Mutual Group will offer the service in coming weeks, it said. GPU Energy, Capstead Mortgage and the Small Business Administration already providing it.

The service presents customers with full-colour, electronic bills including graphics, logos and full billing detail. The information typically printed on the back of a bill is also available for viewing. Once paid, customers can store the bill electronically for future reference.

Customers use the service by going to a central Web site on the Internet to receive bills. The customer will find an electronic check already filled out and waiting for approval and the transaction can be completed with a few clicks of a computer mouse, it said.
CheckFree, based in Atlanta, provides electronic commerce services, software and related products for 1.3 million consumers, 1,000 businesses and 850 financial institutions.
Its stock edged down 6.25 cents to $15.06 on Nasdaq.
